Best AI Tools for Real Estate Professionals: Listings, Outreach and Research

Real estate professionals can use AI to speed up listing copy, outreach, valuation research, and lead follow-up while keeping client trust and local expertise human-led.

By LokkeeVerse Editorial · 17 min read

Best AI Tools for Real Estate Professionals in 2026: Listings, Outreach and Research

Real estate professionals spend much of their time preparing property listings, responding to inquiries, following up with buyers and sellers, researching local markets, and marketing properties across different channels. Managing these responsibilities manually can make it difficult to respond quickly and maintain consistent communication.

Artificial intelligence (AI) tools can help streamline these tasks. They can draft property descriptions, create marketing materials, improve listing photographs, organize client inquiries, automate follow-ups, and support property research.

However, different real estate professionals have different needs. Residential agents may prioritize lead management and listing promotion, commercial brokers may need property intelligence and prospecting tools, while property investors may focus on valuations and market research.

This guide covers 12 AI tools that can support different parts of the real estate workflow, from listing creation and virtual staging to outreach, client management, and property analysis.

What to Look for in AI Tools for Real Estate

Before subscribing to a platform, identify the activities that consume the most time in your business.

  • Listing creation: Can the tool help write property descriptions, promotional emails, and social media captions?
  • Visual marketing: Does it support property photo enhancement, virtual staging, video, or virtual tours?
  • Lead management: Can it organize buyer and seller inquiries and help you prioritize follow-ups?
  • Market research: Does it provide reliable local property data, comparable sales, or market reports?
  • Automation: Can it connect your existing systems and reduce repetitive administrative work?
  • Accuracy and compliance: Can you verify property details, protect client information, and comply with advertising and property regulations?

Real estate data is highly location-dependent. Some property research and CRM platforms focus primarily on the United States, so professionals working in Nigeria or other markets should verify local coverage before subscribing.

1. ChatGPT: Best for Listing Descriptions and Client Communication

ChatGPT is a flexible AI assistant that can help real estate agents prepare property descriptions, write client emails, develop marketing ideas, and summarize research. It can be useful across residential sales, commercial property, property management, and real estate investment.

Rather than starting every document from scratch, professionals can provide verified property information and use AI to create a first draft that they review before publishing.

How real estate professionals can use ChatGPT

  • Drafting descriptions for houses, apartments, land, and commercial properties.
  • Creating buyer and seller email templates.
  • Writing social media captions for new listings.
  • Preparing property viewing follow-up messages.
  • Brainstorming marketing campaigns for specific property types.
  • Organizing notes from property inspections or client conversations.
  • Developing questions for buyer consultations and seller meetings.

For example, an agent marketing a three-bedroom apartment can provide the verified location, floor area, amenities, price, and intended audience. ChatGPT can turn those details into a clear listing description and several social media variations.

The important rule is to supply accurate information. Never allow AI to invent a property's title status, dimensions, amenities, rental income, neighborhood characteristics, or investment returns. Review every description before it reaches a prospective buyer.

ChatGPT is a strong starting point for solo agents and small agencies that need versatile writing and research assistance without immediately purchasing specialized real estate software.

Official website: https://chatgpt.com/

2. ListingAI: Best for Generating Property Listing Copy

ListingAI focuses on generating real estate listing descriptions and related marketing content. It is designed to help property professionals turn basic property details into more polished promotional copy.

This can be useful for agents who handle several properties and need to prepare consistent descriptions without repeating the same writing process each time.

Useful applications

  • Drafting property descriptions from supplied details.
  • Creating alternative versions for different audiences.
  • Improving the clarity and presentation of listing copy.
  • Helping generate marketing language for property advertisements.
  • Reducing the time spent preparing routine listing content.

Imagine an agent listing a two-bedroom apartment for young professionals. The agent can provide the confirmed features and ask for a concise description that emphasizes the property's genuine advantages without making unsupported promises.

ListingAI can help with the writing stage, but it cannot independently verify the condition, ownership, legal status, or market value of a property. Always check the generated copy against the actual property and the rules of the platform where the listing will appear.

It is worth considering if your primary bottleneck is producing property descriptions rather than managing leads or researching market conditions.

Official website: https://www.listingai.co/

3. Canva Magic Studio: Best for Property Marketing Materials

Canva provides design tools for creating promotional graphics, presentations, social media posts, and marketing documents. Its Magic Studio features add AI-assisted capabilities that can help users generate and edit content.

For real estate professionals, Canva is useful for presenting property information consistently across digital and print marketing channels.

What agents can create

  • Property listing flyers.
  • Instagram and Facebook promotional graphics.
  • Open-house announcements.
  • Property brochures and presentations.
  • Branded buyer and seller guides.
  • Social media content for new listings and completed transactions.

For example, an agent can use verified property photographs, a price, the location, and key features to prepare a branded listing graphic. The same design can be adapted into different formats for social platforms, subject to the available design features.

Canva makes content creation easier, but the quality of the final result still depends on the photographs, layout, and accuracy of the information. Review text carefully and avoid using visuals that could misrepresent the property.

It is particularly useful for independent agents and small agencies that need professional-looking marketing materials without hiring a designer for every listing.

Official website: https://www.canva.com/

4. REimagineHome: Best for Virtual Staging and Interior Visualization

REimagineHome provides AI-powered tools for visualizing property interiors and improving real estate marketing images. Virtual staging can help prospective buyers imagine how an empty room might look when furnished.

This can be particularly helpful for vacant properties, investment units, and homes being marketed before physical staging is completed.

How it can support property marketing

  • Virtually staging empty rooms.
  • Exploring alternative interior design styles.
  • Visualizing potential room layouts and furnishings.
  • Preparing more engaging property marketing images.
  • Helping clients understand a property's presentation possibilities.

For example, a property owner selling an unfurnished apartment could use virtual staging to illustrate how the living room might look with furniture and appropriate decor.

Virtual staging is a visualization aid, not evidence of the property's current condition. Clearly disclose digitally staged images where required, retain accurate representations of the actual property, and never digitally conceal material defects or misrepresent permanent features.

Check the provider's current plans, image limits, and commercial-use terms before incorporating the service into a recurring marketing workflow.

Official website: https://www.reimaginehome.ai/

5. BoxBrownie: Best for Property Image Enhancement and Marketing

BoxBrownie offers real estate image editing and visual marketing services, including virtual staging and other property presentation options. It is relevant for agents, property marketers, and developers who need to prepare listing photographs and marketing visuals.

Its services can help improve how a property is presented online, especially when photographs are a major part of attracting prospective buyers.

Potential uses

  • Virtual furniture staging.
  • Editing and enhancing property photographs.
  • Creating visual presentations of spaces.
  • Preparing marketing imagery for vacant or newly developed properties.
  • Supporting a more consistent visual style across listings.

Suppose an agency is marketing a newly completed apartment development. Enhanced photographs and carefully prepared staging visuals can help prospective buyers understand the space and imagine how it could be used.

Visual editing should not create a misleading impression of room dimensions, property condition, views, fixtures, or features. Compare the finished images with the original photographs and follow the relevant listing platform's disclosure requirements.

BoxBrownie is worth evaluating when your business needs polished property visuals but does not want to manage every editing task internally.

Official website: https://www.boxbrownie.com/

6. Matterport: Best for Virtual Property Tours

Matterport specializes in digital property capture and immersive three-dimensional experiences. Its platform helps create virtual tours that allow prospective buyers, tenants, or clients to explore a space remotely.

This can be valuable when a property attracts interest from people who cannot easily attend an in-person viewing.

How real estate professionals can use Matterport

  • Creating immersive virtual property tours.
  • Supporting remote property viewings.
  • Helping buyers understand the layout of a space.
  • Presenting commercial properties to geographically distant clients.
  • Providing digital property documentation for supported workflows.

For example, an agent marketing a commercial office space can provide a virtual tour so prospective tenants can examine the layout before arranging a physical inspection.

Matterport is not simply an AI writing assistant; it is a property visualization platform with a different role in the marketing process. Its suitability depends on the required capture equipment or workflow, subscription, and the value of virtual tours to your target market.

Virtual tours complement rather than replace physical inspections, legal checks, and verification of property measurements.

Official website: https://matterport.com/

7. Follow Up Boss: Best for Real Estate Lead Management

Follow Up Boss is a customer relationship management (CRM) platform designed for real estate teams. It helps agents organize leads, manage communication, and maintain visibility into follow-up activity.

AI and automation capabilities can help teams manage parts of the communication workflow, depending on the available integrations and product features.

What real estate teams can use it for

  • Organizing buyer and seller leads.
  • Tracking contact history and lead status.
  • Coordinating follow-up tasks.
  • Managing communication across a team.
  • Connecting supported lead-generation sources.
  • Monitoring how inquiries progress through the sales pipeline.

Imagine an agency receiving inquiries from its website, property portals, and advertising campaigns. A real estate CRM can help centralize those contacts so agents can review the inquiry, record the next step, and avoid losing track of promising prospects.

A CRM does not automatically generate high-quality leads, and automated follow-ups cannot replace meaningful conversations. Teams should keep contact information accurate, respect communication preferences, and ensure that automated messages remain relevant.

Follow Up Boss is especially worth considering for residential real estate teams that receive enough inquiries to need a dedicated lead management system.

Official website: https://www.followupboss.com/

8. Lofty: Best for Real Estate CRM and Marketing Automation

Lofty is a real estate technology platform that combines CRM, marketing, lead generation, and AI-assisted capabilities. It is designed to help agents and teams manage their client pipeline and coordinate marketing activity.

For businesses that prefer a connected real estate platform rather than multiple disconnected tools, an integrated system may simplify daily operations.

Useful applications

  • Managing buyer and seller relationships.
  • Organizing lead information and follow-up activity.
  • Supporting marketing campaigns.
  • Automating selected communication workflows.
  • Coordinating lead management and related business processes.

For example, a real estate team can use its CRM to track a buyer from the first inquiry through property viewings and subsequent negotiations. Automated reminders and supported AI features can help the team keep communication moving.

The platform's value depends on its fit with your existing process, local market, and preferred integrations. Check the availability of specific AI functions, subscription requirements, and implementation costs before committing.

Lofty is most relevant to teams seeking an integrated real estate CRM and marketing environment rather than a standalone writing tool.

Official website: https://lofty.com/

9. Structurely: Best for Automated Lead Follow-Up

Structurely provides AI-powered conversational lead engagement for businesses, including real estate professionals. It is designed to help respond to incoming leads, ask qualifying questions, and support appointment-setting workflows.

This can be useful when agents receive inquiries outside normal working hours or struggle to follow up with every new contact promptly.

What it can support

  • Engaging incoming leads through supported communication channels.
  • Asking initial qualification questions.
  • Identifying prospects who want further assistance.
  • Supporting appointment-setting workflows.
  • Helping teams prioritize conversations that need human attention.

For example, someone may inquire about a property late at night. An automated assistant can initiate a configured conversation, gather basic information, and help route the inquiry to an agent for follow-up.

Automated conversations should identify themselves appropriately, avoid making unsupported claims, and hand off complex questions to a human. Confirm supported communication channels, integrations, and pricing before adopting the platform.

Structurely is worth considering for agencies with substantial inbound lead volume and a need to improve response coverage.

Official website: https://www.structurely.com/

10. Perplexity: Best for Property and Market Research

Perplexity is an AI-powered research and search platform that can help real estate professionals investigate markets, explore industry information, and locate relevant sources.

It is particularly useful for initial research when an agent needs to understand a new area, prepare a market briefing, or investigate broader property-sector developments.

How professionals can use Perplexity

  • Exploring local market topics through available web sources.
  • Researching development projects and publicly reported announcements.
  • Finding background information on property markets.
  • Preparing initial research notes for client conversations.
  • Identifying sources that need further verification.

For example, an agent entering a new city could use Perplexity to investigate publicly available information about transport projects, commercial developments, and broader housing-market trends before consulting authoritative local data.

Search results may be outdated, incomplete, or irrelevant to a specific transaction. Verify important claims using official property records, planning authorities, credible market reports, and other suitable primary sources.

Perplexity is useful for exploratory research, but it should not be treated as a substitute for a professional valuation or a verified local property database.

Official website: https://www.perplexity.ai/

11. HouseCanary: Best for Property Valuation and Market Analytics

HouseCanary provides property data, valuation analytics, and real estate market intelligence, with a strong focus on the United States. Its tools can support property professionals who need to examine valuation estimates, comparable properties, and market trends.

It is especially relevant to professionals working with US residential property data and investment analysis.

What it can help with

  • Reviewing automated property valuation estimates.
  • Exploring property-level data.
  • Supporting comparative market analysis.
  • Investigating market trends and forecasts.
  • Preparing information for valuation-related discussions.

For example, an agent evaluating a potential listing could use relevant property data and comparable sales to prepare an initial pricing discussion with the seller. The estimate should then be assessed against the property's actual condition, location, unique characteristics, and available market evidence.

Automated valuations are estimates, not guarantees of sale price. They may be less reliable where data is limited or a property is unusual. Verify important figures and use professional judgment when advising clients.

HouseCanary is worth exploring for professionals whose work depends on US property analytics. Agents working in Nigeria or other countries should first establish whether the platform offers sufficient coverage for their target market.

Official website: https://www.housecanary.com/

12. Zapier: Best for Automating Real Estate Workflows

Zapier connects supported applications so that information can move between systems automatically. Its automation and AI-related capabilities can help real estate professionals reduce repetitive administrative work.

Instead of manually copying information from one application to another, teams can create workflows that respond to defined events.

Practical real estate automations

  • Sending a notification when a new inquiry arrives.
  • Creating follow-up tasks from form submissions.
  • Routing leads to the appropriate team member.
  • Connecting supported CRM and marketing applications.
  • Organizing selected property inquiry information.
  • Triggering reminders when an agreed task needs attention.

For example, when a prospective buyer completes an inquiry form, an automation could create a CRM record, notify the assigned agent, and schedule a follow-up task. The agent can then review the request and decide on the appropriate response.

Automation must be configured carefully. Duplicate records, failed integrations, and incorrectly routed leads can damage the customer experience. Test workflows before relying on them and protect personal information as it moves between connected applications.

Zapier is particularly useful for real estate businesses that already use several digital tools and want to connect them without developing every integration from scratch.

Official website: https://zapier.com/

How to Build an AI Workflow for Real Estate

The most effective setup is usually a small group of tools with clearly defined responsibilities. You do not need a separate AI subscription for every activity.

Step 1: Prepare accurate property information

Create a verified record of each property, including its location, price, dimensions, amenities, legal status where applicable, and other relevant details. Use this information as the source for AI-generated marketing materials.

Step 2: Create the listing

Use ChatGPT or ListingAI to draft property descriptions, headlines, and promotional messages. Review the wording and ensure that every factual statement is supported by the property record.

Step 3: Prepare marketing visuals

Use Canva to create branded promotional content. Consider REimagineHome or BoxBrownie for appropriate staging and image-editing needs, and Matterport when immersive virtual tours are valuable to your audience.

Step 4: Publish and manage inquiries

Publish listings on suitable property portals, websites, and social platforms. Route incoming inquiries into a CRM such as Follow Up Boss or Lofty, if it fits your market and budget.

Step 5: Follow up with prospects

Use your CRM's supported automation features or a dedicated tool such as Structurely to help manage initial engagement. Ensure that messages are accurate, relevant, and appropriately handed over to an agent.

Step 6: Research before advising clients

Use Perplexity to discover relevant background sources and consult authoritative local data for important market claims. For US property work, HouseCanary may provide additional property analytics. Always distinguish preliminary research from a formal valuation or professional advice.

Step 7: Measure the results

Track the time spent preparing listings, the speed of responding to inquiries, the number of qualified appointments, and the conversion of leads into clients. Review whether the tools improve actual business outcomes rather than simply increasing the number of automated activities.

Which AI Tools Should Real Estate Professionals Choose?

The right starting point depends on the task you want to improve.

  • For property descriptions and client messages: ChatGPT.
  • For dedicated listing copy: ListingAI.
  • For flyers and marketing graphics: Canva Magic Studio.
  • For virtual staging: REimagineHome.
  • For photo enhancement and property visuals: BoxBrownie.
  • For immersive virtual tours: Matterport.
  • For lead management: Follow Up Boss.
  • For an integrated real estate CRM: Lofty.
  • For automated lead engagement: Structurely.
  • For exploratory market research: Perplexity.
  • For US property analytics: HouseCanary.
  • For connecting apps and automating workflows: Zapier.

These tools serve different purposes and should not be treated as interchangeable. Their features, integrations, regional coverage, and prices may change, so confirm current details with each provider before purchasing.

Important Considerations When Using AI in Real Estate

AI can make property marketing and administration more efficient, but inaccurate information can damage client trust and create legal or financial risks.

  • Verify every property detail before publishing an AI-generated listing.
  • Disclose virtual staging or materially altered images where required.
  • Never use AI to invent rental returns, comparable sales, legal status, or investment guarantees.
  • Protect buyer, seller, tenant, and landlord information.
  • Check local rules on advertising, property transactions, privacy, and fair housing where applicable.
  • Treat automated valuations as estimates and verify them with appropriate market evidence.
  • Review automated messages before sending them to clients, especially when discussing price, availability, or contractual matters.

AI should support professional judgment rather than replace inspections, legal due diligence, reliable valuation methods, or direct communication with clients.

Final Thoughts

The best AI tools for real estate professionals are those that improve the parts of the business where time is frequently lost. Writing assistants can accelerate listing preparation, visual tools can improve property presentation, CRMs can organize leads, and automation platforms can reduce repetitive follow-up work.

Start with one clear priority. If listings take too long to prepare, begin with a writing or design tool. If inquiries are being missed, improve your CRM and follow-up workflow. If your clients need better property information, invest in reliable local data and research processes.

A focused, well-managed toolkit can help real estate professionals work more efficiently while maintaining accurate listings, responsive communication, and trustworthy client relationships.
